questions.question:
Select the combination of signs that when sequentially placed in the given blanks will make the equation correct.

7 _ 3 _ 4 _ 12 _ 6 = 19
questions.solution:
BODMAS rule:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/55cf23d9dc22fa10bb56199cdce71fa3db375d290968e0676171f8d7e9ba3655.png] 

First we will check all the options as:

1) ×, -, +, ÷

Applying the signs, we will get,

⇒ 7 × 3 - 4 + __**12 ÷ 6**__ = 19

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

⇒ __**7 **____**×**____** 3**__ - 4 + 2 = 19

⇒ __**21 - 4 + 2**__ = 19

⇒ 19 = 19, is possible

2) ÷, ×, +, -

Applying the signs, we will get,

⇒ __**7 ÷ 3**__ × 4 + 12 - 6 = 19

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

⇒ __**2.33 ×**____** 4**__ + 12 - 6 = 19

⇒ __**9.32 + 12 - 6**__ = 19

⇒ 15.32 ≠ 19, is not possible

3) -, ×, +, ÷

Applying the signs, we will get,

⇒ 7 - 3 × 4 + __**12 ÷ 6**__ = 19

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

⇒ 7 - __**3 **____**×**____** 4**__ + 2 = 19

⇒ __**7 - 12 + 2**__ = 19

⇒ -3 ≠ 19, is not possible

4) +, ÷, ×, -

Applying the signs, we will get,

⇒ 7 + __**3 ÷ 4**__ × 12 - 6 = 19

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

⇒ 7 + __0.75** ×**____** 12**__ - 6 = 19

⇒ __**7 + 9 - 6**__ = 19

⇒ 10 ≠19, is not possible

Thus, the combination of signs '**×, -, +, ÷**' placed in the given blanks will make the equation correct.

Hence, the correct answer is '__**option 1**__'.

questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

22 - 16 ÷ (3 × 4) + 6 = 8
questions.solution:
BODMAS rule:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab9003ba65914e9db049e6f510b5740718252ca1bdf98a9ac303e65c8cd29d3e.png] 

First we will check all the options as:

1) - and ×

Applying the signs we will get,

⇒ 22 × 16 ÷ (__**3 - 4**__) + 6 = 8

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

⇒ 22 × __**16 ÷ (-1)**__ + 6 = 8

⇒ __**22 **____**×**____** (-16)**__ + 6 = 8

⇒ __**352 + 6**__ = 8

⇒ 358 ≠ 8, is not possible

2) ÷ and ×

Applying the signs we will get,

⇒ 22 - 16 × (__**3 ÷ 4**__) + 6 = 8 

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

⇒ 22 - __**16 × (0.75)**__ + 6 = 8

⇒ __**22 - 12 + 6**__ = 8

⇒ 16 ≠ 8, is not possible

3) ÷ and +

Applying the signs we will get,

⇒ 22 - 16 + (__**3 × 4**__) ÷ 6 = 8 

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

⇒ 22 - 16 + __**(12) ÷ 6**__ = 8

⇒ __**22 - 16 + 2**__ = 8 

⇒ 8 = 8, is possible

4) - and +

Applying the signs we will get,

⇒ 22 + 16 ÷ __**(3 × 4)**__ - 6 = 8 

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

⇒ 22 + __**16 ÷ 12**__ - 6 = 8

⇒ 22 + 1.33 - 6 = 8

⇒ 17.33 ≠ 8, is not possible

Thus, two signs '**÷ and +**' should be interchanged to make the following equation correct.

Hence, the correct answer is '__**option 3**__'.

2. Few gentlemen are not fools.

Next, we will check all the conclusion as below:

I. No gentlemen is rich → Not follow → Since it is given in the statement that few gentlemen are rich.

II. Few gentlemen being fools is a possibility → Follow → Since it is given that few gentlemen are not fools and this means that few are fools is a possibility.

III. No one is both a fool and rich → Not follows → Since it is given that everyone is either a fool or rich but not both.

 

Thus, **o****nly conclusion II** follows.

Hence, the correct answer is '__**option 2**__'.

questions.question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G went to a restaurant for dinner. All of them contributed to the bill. Each person paid a different amount. C paid more than only E, and F paid more than A. B paid less than A. D paid the highest amount, and E paid the least amount. If G paid more than two persons in the group, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: F paid less than D but more than C
A was among the lowest four payers
G paid more than E but less than C
B paid less than D and G

questions.solution:
Seven people went to the restaurant, A, B, C, D, E, F, and G, and paid different bill amounts.

__
 
• ___ > ___ > ___ > ___ > ___ > ___ > ____ .
 
• D paid the highest amount, and E paid the least amount

 D __ > ___ > ___ > ___ > ___> ___ >__ E __ . 

__
 
• If G paid more than two persons in the group

 D __ > ___ > ___ > ___ >__ ____**G **__> ___ >__ E __ .

** ** D __ > __ __**__F __** > __ ____**A** __ > **__ B __** >__ G __> ___ >__ E __ .

__
 
• C paid more than only E

 D __ > __ ____F __ > __ ____A __ > **__ B __** >__ ____G __> **__ C __** >__ E __ .

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1.**

questions.question: The sum of Reena's and her father's age is 60 and the difference between their ages is 36. What is Reena's father's age?
questions.solution:
Let the age of father be 'x' and Reena's be 'y'

The sum of their age is 60.

 **x + y = 60** --------- (1)

The difference between their age is 36.

 **x - y = 36** -----------(2)

From, eq. 2 .** x = 36 + y **------- (3)

**Substituting** **eq. 3** in **eq. 1**

 **36 + y** + y = 60

 2y = __**60 - 36**__

 2y = 24

 **y = 12**

**Substituting** the value of **y** in **eq. 1** 

 x + y = 60

 x + 12 = 60

 x = __**60 - 12**__

 **x = 48 ; y = 12**

 Therefore, Reena's father's age is 48.

Hence, the correct answer is **'****48'.**

B is sitting to the immediate left of D.
C is sitting to the immediate right of D
A and B are sitting next to each other.

questions.solution:
Four friends are sitting in a row facing **north**.

**1. B is at one end**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9554584445676edc028473ddf3d022c4adadbadad569f7c0ee160edf3c6486e4.png] 

 **2. D is between B and C**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c48941ff04a19ae3e8aa30c118cb6769cef3a0fa30cbd2441389b4ba9a8903b.png] 

 **3. A is second to the right of D** (fig. b gets canceled)

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6095c51748ece8b8947c7adcea7b3ed214ae144f2818c20c1efb43c8680bbb26.png] 

According to the arrangements,

Statement 1: A is sitting at one end ⇒ **True**

Statement 2: B is sitting to the immediate left of D ⇒ **True**

Statement 3: C is sitting to the immediate right of D ⇒ **True**

Statement 4: A and B are sitting next to each other ⇒ **False**

Hence, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question: In a college, the total number of students who opted for Biology or Chemistry are 150. Later, 12 students who opted for Biology changed their preference and opted for Chemistry. Now, the number of students in Biology are half the number of students in Chemistry. How many students are in Chemistry now?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

B + C = 150

(B-12) +(C+12) = 150

B-12 = 0.5(C+12)

B = number of students in biology

C = number of students in chemistry

**Solution:**

B - 12 = 0.5C + 6

B = 0.5C + 18

Now, let's put the value of B in the first equation formed.

0.5C + 18 + C = 150

1.5C = 132

C = 132/1.5 = 88

Since, 12 students shifted from biology to chemistry,

**the numbers of students in chemistry now = 88 = 12 = 100**

questions.question: In a fancy dress party of 200 people, 30% of the guests have dressed as animals. 40% of the remaining guests have dressed as birds. 50% of the remaining guests have dressed as clowns. The remaining guests have dressed as plants. How many guests are dressed as plants?
questions.solution:
From the information given:**
Step 1: Out of 200 people, 30% of the guests have dressed as animals.

Dressed as animal = 30% of 200 = 60 people

People left = 200 - 60 = 140

Step 2: 40% of the remaining guests have dressed as birds.

Dressed as birds = 40% of 140 = 56

People left = 140 - 56 = 84

Step 3: 50% of the remaining guests have dressed as clowns.

Dressed as clowns = 50% of 84 = 42

Step 4: The remaining guests have dressed as plants.

**Peoples left = 42**

Hence the correct answer is option 3)**

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements are true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

1. All colours are reds.

2. Some reds are greens.

3. All greens are dark.

Conclusions:

I. All colours being dark is a possibility

II. Some reds are dark.

III. Some reds are colours.
questions.solution:
__**Venn Diagram**__:

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc645a6a734b1ea9ee1619a93b59e25b1b3965baeffe33fba8bafb045df909b7.png] 

__**Conclusion**__:

I. All colours being dark is a possibility ⇒ Follow ⇒** **(All colours can be dark because it is a possibility)

II. Some reds are dark ⇒ Follow ⇒** **(Some green are reds and all green are part of dark, so some reds are dark)

III. Some reds are colours ⇒ Follow ⇒** **(All colours are red, so definitely some reds are colours)

Hence, the correct answer is **'All conclusions follow'**.
